speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. Can you tell me how old the child is and if there have been any recent infections or fever? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC).

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That doctor's assessment of pneumonia doesn't match your symptoms of frequent nosebleeds and petechiae, which are signs of a bleeding disorder rather than a lung infection. To clarify the situation, can you describe how the petechiae appeared on your skin and whether you notice any gum bleeding or blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Smear and Coagulation Profile (PT/PTT/INR).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral_Blood_Smear: {'Findings': 'No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells.'}; Coagulation_Profile: {'PT': '12 seconds (normal)', 'aPTT': '30 seconds (normal)'}

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; they are reassuring so far, but the bleeding symptoms persist. Has the child noticed any family members with similar bleeding issues, and do you notice bleeding after minor bumps or dental procedures? REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and von Willebrand Factor assay.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT)
Given the normal platelet count and coagulation profile alongside your history of frequent nosebleeds, pneumonia likely resulting from alveolar hemorrhage, and petechiae, this pattern strongly suggests a vascular disorder like HHT. Do you notice small, red, spider-like spots on your lips, fingers, or nose?
